title: Optimizing TiO 2  loading in polylactic acid matrices: kinetic and isothermal studies for industrial dye remediation
content: To address the urgent need for sustainable wastewater remediation, this study evaluates the influence of titanium dioxide (TiO2) loading in polylactic acid (PLA) nanocomposites for removing cationic (methylene blue, MB) and anionic (methyl orange, MO) dyes. Sol–gel synthesized TiO2 nanoparticles were incorporated into PLA films at 0.5, 1, and 2 wt% via solvent casting, then characterized using FTIR, SEM, and TGA. Batch tests showed efficient adsorption at pH 10 for MB and pH 3 for MO. For MB, maximum removal efficiencies for bare TiO2, PLA/TiO2-0.5 wt%, PLA/TiO2-1 wt%, and PLA/TiO2-2 wt% were 61%, 86%, 94%, and 73%, respectively. For MO, corresponding efficiencies were 59%, 81%, 87%, and 64%. Adsorption equilibria and dynamics were best described by the Freundlich isotherm and pseudo-second-order kinetics. Ultimately, PLA/TiO2-1 wt% exhibited the highest removal capacity for both dyes, demonstrating that optimizing TiO2 content is critical to prevent performance loss. These findings establish PLA/TiO2-1 wt% as a highly promising, sustainable adsorbent for industrial dye wastewater treatment.
